chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Muhammad ibn Qays, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

Our companions mentioned a people, so I said, 'By Allah, I do not have lunch or dinner except that two or three, or fewer or more, of them are with me.' He (peace be upon him) said: 'Their grace upon you is greater than your grace upon them.' I said, 'May I be your ransom, how is that, while I feed them my food, and spend from my wealth upon them, and my servant serves them?' He (peace be upon him) said: 'When they come to you, they come with abundant sustenance from Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, and when they leave, they leave with forgiveness for you.'
ai.seo_question: Why is hosting guests considered more beneficial for the host than for the guest in Shia hadith?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Al-Kafi*, Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies that the honor of hosting guests stems from their status as vessels of divine blessing rather than mere recipients of charity. While the host expends material wealth, the guests carry the weight of *Rizq* (sustenance) and *Maghfirah* (forgiveness) from Allah, transforming a social act into a spiritual transaction. This reflects the Shia emphasis on *Ihsan* (excellence in conduct) where the guest's presence is viewed as a direct conduit for divine grace upon the household.

en.hubeali:
Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from Muhammad Bin Qays, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup>, said,

‘Our companions mentioned a people, so I said, ‘By Allah<sup>azwj</sup>! I neither have lunch nor dinner except that with me are two from them, or three, or less or more’. So he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘Their grace upon you is more than your grace upon them’. I said, ‘May I be sacrificed for you<sup>asws</sup>! How can that be, and I feed them my food, and I spend upon them from my wealth, and my servants serve them’. So he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘When they come over to you, then enter with a lot of sustenance from Allah<sup>azwj</sup> Mighty and Majestic, and when they go out, they exit with the Forgiveness for you’.
en.sarwar: 4. Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from his father from ibn abu ‘Umayr from Muhammad ibn Qays who has said the following:

“Our people once mentioned a people and I said, ‘By Allah, I do not take lunch or dinner without one two or three of them or more or less with me.’ Abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, then said, ‘Their favor to you is more than your favor to them/ I then said, ‘I pray to Allah to keep my soul in service for your cause, how does that happen? I feed them my food, spend on them from my assets and my servants serve them/ He (the Imam) said, ‘When they come to you they come with sustenance from Allah, most Majestic, most Glorious, and when they leave they leave forgiveness for you/”
